items.title: Sanctioned vessels breach US naval blockade of Iran

featured_image.name: Here's the latest tanker traffic in Strait of Hormuz

items.description: At least two sanctioned cargo vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz and reached Iranian waters on Thursday despite the U.S. Navy's blockade of Iranian ports, raising questions about the effectiveness of enforcement now entering its fourth day.

items.title: Study outlines four options for saving Venice from rising seas

featured_image.name: MOSE flood barrier protects venice - see how it works

items.description:
A team of European researchers has laid out four possible futures for Venice — ranging from reinforcing its existing flood defenses to abandoning the city entirely — warning that without early action, the iconic UNESCO World Heritage Site could be lost within centuries.

The study, published Wednesday in the journal Scientific Reports, was led by oceanographer Piero Lionello of the University of Salento in Italy. It presents what the authors call an "adaptation pathways" framework, mapping out which strategies remain viable as sea levels climb under different emissions scenarios drawn from the IPCC's Sixth Assessment Report.[1][2]

items.title: NASA probe detects surprise solar explosion behavior

featured_image.name: Nasa flies close to Sun, uncovers new clue to how solar storms are ...

items.description: NASA announced Wednesday that its Parker Solar Probe detected a surprise explosion near the Sun, revealing that different particles are flung into space in unexpectedly different ways during the magnetic events that power solar storms.[1][2]

items.title: Lebanon death toll reaches 2,196 as Israeli strikes continue

featured_image.name: Israeli raids displace a quarter of Lebanon's population

items.description:
Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health confirmed on Thursday that the cumulative death toll from Israeli military operations has risen to 2,196, with 7,185 others wounded since the conflict with Hezbollah erupted on March 2, according to the ministry's daily report from its Health Emergency Operations Center. In the past 24 hours alone, at least 29 people were killed and 124 wounded in strikes across southern and eastern Lebanon, Anadolu Agency reported.[1][2][3]

The escalating toll prompted Imran Riza, the UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator for Lebanon, to warn that the human cost has "crossed a devastating threshold," noting more than 2,000 killed and 1.2 million displaced.[4]

items.title: China activates 60,000-chip AI science cluster built without US tech

featured_image.name: China activates largest scientific AI computing cluster in ...

items.description: China activated its largest artificial intelligence computing cluster for scientific research on Tuesday in Zhengzhou, central Henan province, doubling the facility's chip count from 30,000 to 60,000 domestically produced AI accelerators in just two months. The expansion, carried out entirely without American technology, marks a milestone in Beijing's drive for self-sufficiency in advanced computing amid tightening U.S. export controls.[1][2]

items.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to 10-day ceasefire, Trump says

featured_image.name: Donald Trump Announces Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Thursday that Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 10-day ceasefire set to take effect at 5 p.m. EST, pausing weeks of devastating Israeli strikes against Hezbollah that have killed more than 2,000 people in Lebanon since early March.

"These two Leaders have agreed that in order to achieve PEACE between their Countries, they will formally begin a 10 Day CEASEFIRE at 5 P.M. EST," Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the agreement followed "excellent" conversations with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.[1][2][3]

Trump said he would invite both leaders to the White House for what he called "the first meaningful talks between Israel and Lebanon since 1983." He also said he had directed Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio to work with both countries toward "a Lasting PEACE."[4][5][6]

items.title: IMF says Asia faces worst exposure to Middle East energy shock

featured_image.name: India's Economy

items.description: The International Monetary Fund warned on Thursday that Asia is more exposed than any other region to the energy shock unleashed by the war in the Middle East, as the fund's spring meetings in Washington laid bare the widening economic toll of the conflict on the world's poorest nations.

items.title: Trump says Iran agreed to hand over enriched uranium as deal nears

featured_image.name: Iran war 'very close to over,' Trump says — and the stock market 'is going to boom'

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared Thursday that Iran has agreed to relinquish its stockpile of enriched uranium, claiming the two sides are "close" to a peace deal to end over six weeks of war. The assertion came as Reuters reported that U.S. and Iranian negotiators have scaled back ambitions for a comprehensive agreement and are instead pursuing a temporary memorandum to prevent a return to hostilities before the ceasefire expires on April 21.[1][2]

A separate source told Reuters that Iran had agreed to dilute its highly enriched uranium under the supervision of the International Atomic Energy Agency and the United States. A senior Iranian lawmaker, Ali Nikzad, the deputy speaker of parliament, said earlier this week that Tehran had agreed to dilute 450 kilograms of enriched uranium as a goodwill measure, though he added that the United States later backed out of that arrangement.[3][4][5]

items.title: White House clears path for federal agencies to use Anthropic's Mythos AI

featured_image.name: White House Moves to Give US Agencies Anthropic Mythos ...

items.description:
The White House Office of Management and Budget is establishing security protocols to allow major federal agencies to begin using Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview, the powerful AI model that has rattled cybersecurity experts and financial regulators on both sides of the Atlantic since its limited release earlier this month. Federal CIO Gregory Barbaccia informed Cabinet departments of the plan, according to a memo reviewed by Bloomberg.[1]

The move comes even as government officials grapple with the model's potential to sharply increase cybersecurity risk — and despite an ongoing legal and political clash between the Trump administration and Anthropic over the use of the company's AI technology.

items.title: Pope Leo decries world 'ravaged by tyrants' amid feud with Trump

featured_image.name: Pope Leo decries world ravaged by 'tyrants' in speech ...

items.description: Pope Leo XIV delivered some of his most forceful remarks yet on Thursday, declaring that the world is "being ravaged by a handful of tyrants" during a peace gathering in the conflict-scarred city of Bamenda, Cameroon. The address, made at Saint Joseph Cathedral on the second day of his Cameroon visit, came amid an escalating public feud with U.S. President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance over the pontiff's opposition to the war in Iran.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump announces Israel-Lebanon ceasefire as oil holds near $95

featured_image.name: Donald Trump Announces Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire

items.description:
Oil prices moved higher on Thursday as investors weighed a new ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon alongside expectations for a second round of peace talks between the United States and Iran, the two dynamics shaping a conflict that has roiled energy markets for nearly seven weeks.

West Texas Intermediate crude rose more than 2 percent on the day, according to Trading Economics, while Brent crude held near $95 to $97 per barrel. The modest gains came after a volatile stretch that saw prices swing sharply in the aftermath of collapsed negotiations between Washington and Tehran last weekend.[1][2][3]

items.title: Cuba's Diaz-Canel vows to fight any US attack as Pentagon ramps up planning

featured_image.name: Cuba's president says island does not wish for US aggression

items.description:
Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel warned on Thursday that Cuba is prepared to confront a potential military attack from the United States, delivering the message at a rally in Havana commemorating the 65th anniversary of the declaration of the Cuban Revolution's socialist character. "The moment is extremely challenging and calls upon us once again, as on April 16, 1961, to be ready to confront serious threats, including military aggression. We do not want it, but it is our duty to prepare to avoid it and, if it becomes inevitable, to defeat it," Díaz-Canel told hundreds of supporters, according to the Associated Press.[1]

The speech came days after President Donald Trump suggested his administration could turn its attention to Cuba once the war in Iran concludes. "We may stop by Cuba after we finish with this," Trump said earlier this week, describing the island as a "failing nation."[2][1]

items.title: Gold rises as U.S.-Iran peace talk hopes lift markets

featured_image.name: Gold gains on revived rate cut bets as Iran peace hopes ... - CNBC

items.description:
Gold prices climbed on Thursday as renewed optimism about a diplomatic resolution to the U.S.-Iran conflict eased inflation concerns and bolstered expectations for eventual interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve.

Spot gold rose roughly 0.7% in early trading, while the U.S. dollar slipped to a six-week low and benchmark 10-year Treasury yields edged lower, according to Reuters. The combination made gold more attractive to holders of other currencies and reduced the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding metal.[1]

items.title: Slovakia vows to block EU Russia sanctions over Druzhba pipeline dispute

featured_image.name: Slovakia plans to block 20th EU sanctions package against Russia ...

items.description:
Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanár announced on Thursday that Slovakia will block the European Union's 20th sanctions package against Russia until it receives clear and verifiable guarantees that oil flows through the Druzhba pipeline will resume, according to Slovakia's Dennik N newspaper. In a notable departure from Hungary's earlier blanket obstruction, Bratislava said it will not oppose the EU's €90 billion loan to Ukraine.[1][2][3][4]

"If the Druzhba pipeline does not function, and the issue of approving the 20th package is discussed, we will not approve it, because we have no other tools than to force Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, together with the European Commission, to launch the Druzhba pipeline," Blanár told a parliamentary committee on European affairs.[4]

items.title: US expands Iran blockade to target sanctioned ships worldwide

featured_image.name: US military says it will start blockade of all ships going ...

items.description:
The United States has extended the scope of its naval blockade against Iran, authorizing forces to search and seize not only vessels traveling to and from Iranian ports but also OFAC-sanctioned ships and suspected dark fleet vessels operating anywhere in the world, according to an update from U.S. Naval Forces Central Command reported by Seatrade Maritime on Thursday.[1][2]

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Air Force Gen. Dan Caine outlined the expanded posture at a Pentagon briefing Thursday morning, as the blockade entered its fourth day with no vessels having successfully breached the cordon, according to U.S. Central Command.[3][4][5]

items.title: Trump announces 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon

featured_image.name: default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C234%2C4500%2C2531%29%3BResize%3D1280

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Thursday that Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 10-day ceasefire, set to begin at 5 p.m. Eastern Time, in a declaration made on his Truth Social platform. Trump said the agreement followed "excellent conversations" with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, marking a rapid escalation in diplomatic efforts to de-escalate a six-week-old war that has killed more than 2,000 people and displaced over a million in Lebanon.[1][2]

Trump said he has directed Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine to work with both countries to "achieve a lasting peace." However, as of Thursday morning, neither the Israeli government nor Hezbollah had formally confirmed the truce, and the agreement notably excludes the Iran-backed militant group that has been exchanging fire with Israeli forces across southern Lebanon.[3][2][1]

items.title: Study projects Atlantic current system to weaken 51% by 2100

featured_image.name: Shifting Gulf Stream may signal an ocean current collapse is next

items.description:
A wave of recent research has intensified warnings that the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation — the vast system of ocean currents that regulates climate across the Northern Hemisphere — is weakening faster than climate models predicted and may be approaching a point of no return.

A study published April 14 in Science Advances by Valentin Portmann and colleagues projects that the AMOC will weaken by roughly 51 percent by the end of this century, a slowdown approximately 60 percent stronger than suggested by the average of current climate models. The research combined observational data with climate model outputs to constrain projections, finding that models alone have been underestimating the severity of the decline.[1][2]

items.title: Industrial chemical leaks could delay ozone recovery by 7 years, study finds

featured_image.name: NASA: Ozone layer hole shrinks to smallest size since discovery

items.description:
A regulatory exemption in the Montreal Protocol — widely regarded as the most successful international environmental treaty — could push back the full recovery of the ozone layer by about seven years, according to a study published Wednesday in Nature Communications.[1]

An international team of scientists found that industrial chemicals still permitted as raw materials under the treaty are leaking into the atmosphere at rates far higher than previously assumed, threatening to undermine decades of progress in healing the ozone layer.[2][3]

items.title: IMF says Middle East war is testing Asia's economic resilience

featured_image.name: IMF chief's warning: No painless exit from war's energy shock - Axios

items.description: The International Monetary Fund warned on Wednesday that Asia's heavy dependence on Middle Eastern oil and gas leaves the region acutely exposed to the energy shock unleashed by the war in the Middle East, even as it urged governments to resist broad fuel subsidies that could worsen inflation and strain already elevated public debt.

items.title: Pakistan pushes for new US-Iran talks as Hormuz blockade batters India's economy

featured_image.name: Global oil supply, economic growth face severe hit from ...

items.description: The United States naval blockade of Iranian ports, now entering its fourth day, is sending shockwaves through the global economy and posing an acute threat to India's energy security, as mediators scramble to restart peace talks between Washington and Tehran.
